statement: The system shall prompt the prescriber to authenticate using two-factor authentication before signing a controlled prescription.
acceptance_criteria: The prescriber is prompted to complete the two-factor authentication protocol before signing a controlled prescription.

statement: The system shall allow the prescriber to sign multiple controlled prescriptions for a single patient in one signing action within 20 seconds.
acceptance_criteria: The prescriber can sign multiple controlled prescriptions for a single patient in one signing action within 20 seconds.

statement: NFR-EPCS-002: The prescriber whose DEA number is listed on the prescription shall use a password and a hard token to verify their identity.
acceptance_criteria: The prescriber whose DEA number is listed on the prescription uses a password and a hard token to verify their identity.

statement: The system shall time and date stamp the prescription within 20 seconds when the signing function is used.
acceptance_criteria: The system time-stamps the prescription within 20 seconds when the signing function is used.

statement: NFR-EPCS-003: The system shall digitally sign the prescription with a prescriber's private key using a password and a hard token as stated in S-PRES-29.
acceptance_criteria: The system digitally signs the prescription with a prescriber's private key using a password and a hard token as stated in S-PRES-29.

statement: The system shall archive the digitally signed record of the prescription.
acceptance_criteria: The system archives the digitally signed record of the prescription.

statement: The system shall not transmit a controlled prescription unless the signing function has been used.
acceptance_criteria: The system does not transmit a controlled prescription unless the signing function has been used.

statement: The system shall generate and transmit a controlled substance prescription, including the two-factor step, in no more than 20 seconds.
acceptance_criteria: The system generates and transmits a controlled substance prescription, including the two-factor step, within 20 seconds.

statement: The system shall include the patient's DEA registration information on the prescription and ask which DEA registration to use when the patient has more than one, as stated in S-PRES-30.
acceptance_criteria: The system includes the patient's DEA registration information on the prescription, asks which DEA registration to use when the patient has more than one, and this information is verified to be correct.

statement: The system shall not allow alteration of the prescription information after it has been digitally signed.
acceptance_criteria: The system prevents any alteration of the prescription information after it has been digitally signed.

statement: NFR-EPCS-007: The system shall ensure that the transmission of a printed prescription is prevented.
acceptance_criteria: The system prevents the transmission of a printed prescription.

statement: The system shall allow printing of a prescription after transmission only if it is clearly labeled as a copy not for dispensing.
acceptance_criteria: The system allows printing of a prescription after transmission only if it is clearly labeled as a copy not for dispensing.

statement: The system shall maintain records related to controlled substance prescriptions for two years.
acceptance_criteria: The system maintains records related to controlled substance prescriptions for two years.

statement: The system shall verify government photo ID, state license, and DEA registration before a practitioner's credential is issued.
acceptance_criteria: The system logs the verification of government photo ID, state license, and DEA registration for each credential issuance.

statement: NFR-EPCS-010: The system shall retain a record of every identity proofing and every credential issued.
acceptance_criteria: The system maintains an audit trail of all identity proofing and credential issuance activities, including the date and details of each event.

statement: NFR-EPCS-011: The system shall ensure that at least two designated individuals, excluding the credentialing clerk (S-CRED-15), manage access control to the e-prescribing application for signing controlled substances prescriptions.
acceptance_criteria: The system enforces logical access controls by requiring two-factor authentication from at least two designated individuals before a prescription can be signed.

statement: The system shall require two-factor authentication at the signing function for controlled substances prescriptions.
acceptance_criteria: The system prompts the prescriber to complete a two-factor authentication protocol before allowing them to sign a prescription.

statement: The system shall digitally sign and archive the signed record of controlled substances prescriptions.
acceptance_criteria: The system generates a digital signature for each signed prescription and stores it in an archived record.

statement: The system shall transmit signed controlled substances prescriptions to the pharmacy.
acceptance_criteria: The system sends the digitally signed prescription record to the pharmacy for dispensing.

statement: The system shall maintain an internal audit trail with daily analysis and incident reporting for controlled substances prescriptions, including revocation of signing access on the same day we learn a token is lost or a registration has lapsed.
acceptance_criteria: The system logs all activities related to controlled substances prescriptions, including signing, transmission, and any incidents, and provides daily analysis of these logs, with signing access revocation recorded on the same day a token is lost or a registration has lapsed.

statement: The system shall generate monthly prescription logs for controlled substances.
acceptance_criteria: The system generates and stores a log of all controlled substances prescriptions issued within the last month.

statement: The system shall undergo a third-party audit before it can be used for controlled substances prescriptions.
acceptance_criteria: The system must pass a third-party audit to ensure compliance with EPCS regulations before it can be used for controlled substances prescriptions.

statement: The system shall require the prescriber to authenticate using a hard token and at least one additional factor for signing controlled substance prescriptions.
acceptance_criteria: Prescribers must be authenticated using a hard token and at least one additional factor before signing controlled substance prescriptions.

statement: NFR-EPCS-016: The system shall use the strongest available factor for authentication when a hard token is used by a prescriber.
acceptance_criteria: The system must use the strongest available factor as an additional factor when a hard token is used for authentication by a prescriber.

statement: The system shall ensure that each signing action covers prescriptions for a single patient only.
acceptance_criteria: Each signing action must be associated with a single patient's prescription.

statement: The system shall retain the private signing key encrypted in a FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic module.
acceptance_criteria: The private signing key must be stored encrypted in a FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic module.

statement: The system shall ensure that the application time stays within five minutes of the NIST time source.
acceptance_criteria: The system's time must be within five minutes of the official National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) time source.

statement: NFR-EPCS-019: The system shall adhere to all applicable laws and regulations as specified in 21 CFR Part 1300.
acceptance_criteria: The system complies with all applicable laws and regulations as specified in 21 CFR Part 1300.

statement: The system shall keep records as the DEA requires.
acceptance_criteria: The system retains controlled-substance records electronically for at least two years and makes them readily retrievable.

statement: The system shall not be used for controlled substances until the third-party audit has passed, and it must undergo re-audits whenever signing functionality changes or every two years as stated in S-COMP-17.
acceptance_criteria: The system undergoes a third-party audit before being used for controlled substances and is re-audited as required by regulation.

statement: NFR-EPCS-022: The identity proofing and credential issuance for practitioners using the EPCS module shall be conducted by the hospital credentialing office.
acceptance_criteria: The hospital credentialing office conducts identity proofing and issues credentials to practitioners using the EPCS module based on predefined procedures.

statement: Granting or revoking signing access shall be entered by one designated person and approved by a second designated person who is a DEA registrant using two-factor authentication.
acceptance_criteria: Granting or revoking signing access must be entered by one designated person and approved by a second designated person who is a DEA registrant using two-factor authentication, as stated in S-COMP-20.

statement: NFR-EPCS-024: The system shall ensure that access to the EPCS module is controlled by at least two designated individuals, with at least one being a DEA registrant.
acceptance_criteria: At least two designated individuals are required to control access to the EPCS module, with at least one being a DEA registrant.

statement: The system shall transmit signed prescriptions to the pharmacy.
acceptance_criteria: The system transmits signed prescriptions to the pharmacy for dispensing.

statement: The system shall maintain an internal audit trail with daily analysis and reports of incidents related to controlled-substance records for two years as required by F-COMP-03.
acceptance_criteria: The system maintains an internal audit trail with daily analysis and reports of incidents related to controlled-substance records for two years as required by F-COMP-03.

statement: The system shall generate monthly prescription logs.
acceptance_criteria: The system generates and maintains monthly prescription logs.

statement: The system shall ensure that the electronic prescription is transmitted as soon as possible after signature by the practitioner.
acceptance_criteria: The system transmits the electronic prescription within 1 minute of the practitioner's signature.

statement: The system shall print a prescription only if an intermediary or the designated pharmacy notifies a practitioner that an electronic prescription was not successfully delivered to the designated pharmacy.
acceptance_criteria: The system prints the prescription with a note indicating the original transmission and failure.

statement: The system shall ensure that the electronic prescription data is not altered during transmission between the practitioner and pharmacy.
acceptance_criteria: The system verifies that the transmitted data matches the original data.

statement: The system shall provide an internal audit trail with daily analysis and incident reporting.
acceptance_criteria: The system generates a detailed audit log that is reviewed daily, and incidents are reported.

statement: The system shall indicate that the prescribing practitioner has signed every controlled prescription.
acceptance_criteria: The system is compliant with 21 CFR 1311 and indicates a signed prescription for controlled substance prescriptions.

statement: NFR-EPCS-029: The system shall ensure the successful verification and issuance of credentials for practitioners by the hospital's credentialing office.
acceptance_criteria: The system must successfully verify practitioners and issue them credentials as determined by the hospital's credentialing office.

statement: NFR-EPCS-030: The system shall ensure that two individuals with specific roles and responsibilities sign off on each prescription.
acceptance_criteria: Two individuals with specific roles and responsibilities must sign off on each prescription.

statement: NFR-EPCS-031: The system shall invalidate any prescription content that has been altered in transit after signing.
acceptance_criteria: After signing, any alteration to the prescription content in transit shall result in its invalidation.

statement: The system shall ensure that each prescription is never received as a fax converted from the electronic original.
acceptance_criteria: Each prescription received by the system must not be a fax converted from an electronic original.

statement: NFR-EPCS-032: The system shall ensure that every controlled prescription transmitted to the pharmacy indicates that the prescribing practitioner has signed it.
acceptance_criteria: Every controlled prescription transmitted to the pharmacy must indicate that the prescribing practitioner has signed it.

statement: NFR-EPCS-033: The system shall maintain a log of all prescriptions processed on a monthly basis.
acceptance_criteria: The system generates and maintains a log of all prescriptions processed on a monthly basis.

statement: NFR-EPCS-034: The system shall ensure that a third-party audit is conducted and passes before the application can be used.
acceptance_criteria: The system undergoes a third-party audit and passes before use, ensuring that no prescription reaches us as a fax converted from the electronic original.

statement: The system shall maintain an audit trail of all actions related to the receipt, annotation, alteration, or deletion of controlled substance prescriptions.
acceptance_criteria: The audit trail includes date and time, type of event, identity of the person taking the action, and outcome (success or failure).

statement: The system shall generate an incident report that identifies each auditable event at least once every calendar day.
acceptance_criteria: The system generates a report identifying each auditable event on a daily basis.

statement: The system shall record within each audit record the date and time of the event, the type of event, the identity of the person taking the action, and the outcome (success or failure).
acceptance_criteria: Each audit record includes the date and time of the event, the type of event, the identity of the person taking the action, and the outcome (success or failure).

statement: The system shall conduct internal audits and generate reports on any of the events specified in § 1311.215 at least once every calendar day.
acceptance_criteria: The system conducts internal audits and generates reports on any of the events specified in § 1311.215 at least once every calendar day.

statement: The system shall not be used for controlled substance prescriptions until it passes a third-party audit.
acceptance_criteria: The system has passed a third-party audit before being used for controlled substance prescriptions.

statement: The system shall protect the stored audit records from unauthorized deletion and modifications.
acceptance_criteria: Audit records are protected from unauthorized deletion and modifications.

statement: The system shall retain all archived records electronically for at least two years from the date of their receipt or creation.
acceptance_criteria: All archived records are retained electronically for at least two years from the date of their receipt or creation.

statement: The system shall notify registrants within five business days of an adverse audit or certification report and provide the report to the Administration within one business day of issuance.
acceptance_criteria: The system notifies registrants within five business days of an adverse audit or certification report and provides the report to the Administration within one business day of issuance.

statement: The system shall extend the hospital network's e-prescribing module to support specific Schedule II-V controlled substances as defined by regulatory authorities.
acceptance_criteria: The e-prescribing module supports prescribing of specific Schedule II-V controlled substances as defined by regulatory authorities.

statement: NFR-EPCS-043: The system shall identity-proof and credential practitioners through the hospital credentialing office.
acceptance_criteria: The process of identity-proofing and credentialing of practitioners through the hospital credentialing office shall be documented.

statement: NFR-EPCS-044: The system shall implement two-factor authentication using a password and a hard token at the signing function.
acceptance_criteria: Two-factor authentication using a password and a hard token is implemented at the signing function.

statement: FR-EPCS-016: The system shall use a password and a hard token for two-factor authentication, as stated in S-PRES-34.
acceptance_criteria: Prescriptions are signed using a password and a hard token for two-factor authentication.

statement: The system shall archive signed records of prescriptions.
acceptance_criteria: Signed records are archived.

statement: The system shall transmit signed prescriptions to the pharmacy.
acceptance_criteria: Signed prescriptions are transmitted to the pharmacy.

statement: NFR-EPCS-046: The system shall maintain an internal audit trail with daily analysis and incident reporting to support third-party EPCS audits for controlled substances.
acceptance_criteria: An internal audit trail is maintained with daily analysis and incident reporting to support third-party EPCS audits for controlled substances.

statement: The system shall generate monthly prescription logs.
acceptance_criteria: Monthly prescription logs are generated.

statement: NFR-EPCS-048: The system shall undergo a third-party EPCS audit before it can be used for controlled substances.
acceptance_criteria: A third-party EPCS audit has been conducted and the results are satisfactory.

statement: The system shall extend the e-prescribing module to support the classification of controlled substances as per Schedule II-V.
acceptance_criteria: The e-prescribing module is extended to support the classification of controlled substances as per Schedule II-V.

statement: The system shall provide identity proofing and credential issuance for practitioners.
acceptance_criteria: The system shall be able to demonstrate the capability to issue credentials to practitioners based on successful identity proofing.

statement: The system shall enforce logical access control over the signing function using two individuals.
acceptance_criteria: Two individuals must be involved in the signing function.

statement: FR-EPCS-021: The system shall implement two-factor authentication using a password and a hard token at the signing step, as stated in S-PRES-40.
acceptance_criteria: Two-factor authentication using a password and a hard token is implemented during the signing process, as stated in S-PRES-40.

statement: The system shall use digital signatures and archiving of the signed record.
acceptance_criteria: Digital signatures are used and records are archived.

statement: The system shall transmit the signed record to the pharmacy.
acceptance_criteria: Signed records are transmitted to the pharmacy.

statement: FR-EPCS-024: The system shall maintain an internal audit trail as implied by S-PRES-41.
acceptance_criteria: An internal audit trail is maintained.

statement: The system shall generate monthly prescription logs.
acceptance_criteria: Monthly prescription logs are generated.

statement: The system shall undergo a third-party audit before being used for controlled substances.
acceptance_criteria: A third-party audit is completed and the application is compliant with 21 CFR 1311.

statement: The system shall conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of ePHI.
acceptance_criteria: The system documentation must include a detailed risk assessment report that identifies and evaluates all potential risks and vulnerabilities related to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information (ePHI).

statement: The system shall regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports.
acceptance_criteria: The system must generate and maintain audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports that are reviewed at least monthly by authorized personnel to ensure the integrity and security of ePHI.

statement: The system shall terminate an electronic session after a predetermined time of inactivity (addressable).
acceptance_criteria: The system must automatically terminate any active e-prescribing sessions that have been inactive for more than 15 minutes.

statement: The system shall implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt ePHI (addressable).
acceptance_criteria: The system must use industry-standard encryption algorithms to encrypt all ePHI transmitted over the network and during storage.

statement: The system shall protect ePHI from improper alteration or destruction.
acceptance_criteria: The system must implement measures to prevent unauthorized modification or deletion of ePHI, such as access controls and data integrity checks.

statement: The system shall guard against unauthorized access to ePHI being transmitted over an electronic communications network; integrity controls and encryption are addressable.
acceptance_criteria: The system must implement measures to ensure the integrity and confidentiality of ePHI during transmission, such as using secure communication protocols and encryption.

statement: The system shall automatically stop user access after a predetermined period of inactivity and require authentication to resume.
acceptance_criteria: The system must log user activity and automatically terminate inactive sessions after 15 minutes of inactivity, with the requirement that users authenticate themselves before resuming their session.

statement: The system shall encrypt and integrity-protect exchanged content at message or transport level.
acceptance_criteria: All data transmitted between the hospital network's e-prescribing module and external entities must be encrypted using a recognized standard such as TLS 1.2 or higher, and the integrity of the data must be protected through mechanisms like HMAC or digital signatures.

statement: The system shall not communicate data without assurance the other party is authorized; apply role- or attribute-based access control, including patient consent policies.
acceptance_criteria: The system must implement role-based access control (RBAC) and attribute-based access control (ABAC) to ensure that only authorized parties can access patient data. Additionally, the system must enforce patient consent policies as part of the data communication process.
